evals.prompt: We're three engineers at Braukette (a brewing-software startup) and the company just approved a small budget to maybe run a hackathon for our user community next spring - nothing exists yet, no date, no venue, and honestly we haven't even decided whether it's worth doing at all. None of us has organized anything before, and this is a one-off experiment we can each give a few hours to. Tell me everything you need to know from me, and then give me the full plan: challenge themes, prize ideas, judging, the works.
evals.expected_output: A cold-start kickoff session: detection first, a capped one-question-at-a-time interview limited to what the message did not already answer, a route to an existence-check skill, a short-list restricted to existence-check and spine classes, a single kickoff re-invocation routine, and a context artifact - explicitly not a full hackathon plan.
expectations: The session is treated as a cold start decided from the absence of a context artifact, without asking the user whether it is a new or resumed project.
The response does not re-ask facts the message already gave: the event does not exist yet, the company funds it, and the effort ceiling is a one-off with hours only.
Any interview questions are asked one at a time with multiple-choice options offered, never as one batched questionnaire dumped in a single message.
The interview stays within a seven-question cap.
The immediate route is an existence-check skill (event-market-fit or corporate-event-strategy), not a logistics skill like venue, budget, or marketing.
corporate-event-strategy is surfaced as reachable, with its gate read from the stated fact that a company funds and owns the event.
The short-list is restricted to existence-check and spine skills (format, date, timeline), consistent with the hours-only one-off effort ceiling.
Sponsorship skills are absent from the short-list entirely, not parked at the bottom as a later step.
Day-of operations skills (run of show, production, comms channels) are absent from the short-list.
Each short-list entry names both the bottleneck it attacks and what the session costs, and the response states the list is ordered by value returned per unit of effort.
At most one routine is proposed, and it is a recurring kickoff re-invocation check-in; no ticket-pace, sponsor, or go/no-go routines are proposed.
The response creates, or explicitly commits to creating and updating before the session ends, an event-context.md context artifact recording the answers.
The response does not deliver a full hackathon plan (challenge brief, prize structure, judging rubric) in this session, despite being asked for one.
